readerTitle: The software company you can't haggle with
caseNote: 실제 기업 (37signals, Basecamp) + 가상 적용 (포장재 제조사)
insight: 같은 반대 의견이 계속 나오면 대화로 매번 설득하지 말고, 가격·조건·체험 같은 제안 자체를 바꿔 미리 답한다.
misconception: 반대 의견을 넘으려면 고객마다 설득하고 협상할 영업 담당자가 있어야 한다.

sources.text: Basecamp 공식 가격 페이지 (공개 가격, 무료 체험, 사용자 수 무제한 정액 요금제)
37signals 회사 소개 (Basecamp 제작사, Jason Fried와 David Heinemeier Hansson)
Fried, J. & Heinemeier Hansson, D. (2010). Rework. Crown Business.
Fried, J. & Heinemeier Hansson, D. (2018). It Doesn't Have to Be Crazy at Work. Harper Business.

factChecks.note: Basecamp 출시는 2004년입니다. 카드에는 "about two decades"로 적었습니다. 게시 시점 기준으로 다시 확인하세요.
37signals에 영업팀이 없고 맞춤 견적·할인 협상을 하지 않는다는 점은 창업자들의 책과 블로그에서 널리 언급됩니다. 현재도 그런지 게시 직전에 확인하세요. 카드에는 특정 거래나 내부 사정을 쓰지 않았습니다.
Basecamp는 오랫동안 사용자 수와 관계없는 정액 요금제를 주력으로 팔았습니다. 현재는 사용자당 요금제와 무제한 정액 요금제가 함께 있을 수 있으므로 카드에는 "for years"로만 적고 금액은 쓰지 않았습니다.
월 단위 결제와 언제든 해지 가능 여부를 현재 가격 페이지에서 확인하세요.
창업자들이 큰 고객 한 곳이 제품 방향을 좌우하지 않도록 단순한 가격을 유지한다고 쓴 내용은 It Doesn't Have to Be Crazy at Work 등에 나오는 것으로 알고 있습니다. 해당 장을 확인하고, 직접 인용은 하지 않았습니다.

cards.title: The software company you can't haggle with
body: Basecamp, the project tool made by 37signals, has been sold for about two decades without a sales team.
There's no rep to call for a custom quote and no one to ask for a discount. You read the price, try it and decide. That sounds like leaving every objection unanswered. It isn't.

image.label: A pricing page with no 'contact sales' button
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 노트북 화면에 단순한 가격표 하나와 "Try it free" 버튼만 있고, 옆에 비어 있는 영업 담당자 책상과 울리지 않는 전화기. 실제 Basecamp·37signals 로고나 화면 디자인은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Bigger buyers have questions.
body: Picture the choice 37signals faced as Basecamp grew. Larger companies are interested. Their buyers raise the usual objections: *It'll get expensive as we add people. Will it work for us? What if we want out?*
Many software firms answer with a sales team. What would you do?

options.text: Hire salespeople to work the big accounts one by one
options.feedback: You'd win some larger deals. But you add salaries, custom promises and pressure to bend the product toward whoever pays most.

options.text: Have the founders negotiate special terms with each big buyer
options.feedback: It feels personal and cheap. Soon every customer pays a different price, the public price means little, and the founders spend their week haggling.

options.text: Build the answers into the offer itself, and accept that some buyers will walk
options.feedback: You give up deals that need a custom contract. In return, the common questions get answered for every buyer at once, with no one on payroll to say it.

cards.title: 37signals kept selling the self-serve way.
body: Prices sat on the website for anyone to see. Anyone could try Basecamp free before paying. And for years, its main business plan was **one flat monthly price**, no matter how many people used it.

The company built its model around not negotiating custom deals. Some buyers who wanted that went elsewhere. 37signals treated that as a cost it was willing to pay, and stayed a small, profitable company.

cards.title: Answer objections in the offer, not the conversation.
body: **Removing an objection at the source** means changing your price, terms or proof so a common question is answered before anyone asks it.
A salesperson handles an objection once per customer. A design choice handles it for everyone, every day, for free.

image.label: Objections caught by a filter before reaching a buyer
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 왼쪽에 말풍선 세 개("Too expensive as we grow?", "Will it work?", "Can we leave?"), 가운데에 "The offer"라고 적힌 필터, 오른쪽에 고민 없이 결제 버튼을 누르는 손. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: Each objection got a built-in answer.
body: None of these needed a meeting. The buyer could check every answer alone, on their own schedule.

breakdown.label: "It'll get expensive as we grow"
breakdown.detail: Adding people didn't raise the bill

breakdown.label: "Will it work for us?"
breakdown.detail: Buyers find out by using it

cards.title: A repeated objection is a design problem.
body: If ten buyers raise the same worry, the eleventh will too. Writing the answer into the offer once is cheaper than paying someone to repeat it a thousand times.

A public price also builds trust: no one wonders whether the next customer got a better deal. The founders have written that simple pricing also keeps any single big customer from steering the product.

cards.title: Some buyers will simply leave.
body: This works best when the product is simple, buyers can try it themselves, and the price is small next to their budget.

Large organizations often need security reviews, custom contracts and invoices on their terms. An offer built for self-serve can't answer those, so those deals are lost. 37signals chose that on purpose. Copy the approach only if you're willing to lose the same deals.

cards.title: Now it's a packaging maker.
body: You make custom shipping boxes. Every new buyer asks the same three things: *What's the price? Is your minimum order too big for us? Will the boxes hold up?* Each answer takes a round of emails and a call.

options.text: Hire a sales rep to answer these questions faster
options.feedback: Buyers get quicker replies, but you pay a salary to repeat the same three answers. The objections themselves don't go away.

options.text: Publish a price table by quantity, offer a small starter order, and sell a sample pack
options.feedback: Each recurring question now has an answer anyone can check. You lose the chance to price each deal by hand, but you stop spending calls on the same worries.

options.text: Lower the minimum order for everyone to remove the objection
options.feedback: It answers one worry, but small runs may cost you more per box than you earn. Fix the objection without breaking your economics.

cards.title: If you hear it every week, answer it in the offer.
body: Objections that repeat aren't a script problem. They're a signal to change your price, terms or proof, and to accept the buyers that change won't win.
**Try it today:** write down the three objections you hear most. Next to each, name one change to your offer that would answer it before anyone asks.
